hypothesis: Measured on one rented GPU box, the time of one batched GR4J forward pass over 2,684 chains and the matching vectorized CPU time, substituted into the card's own derivation (main_run_hours = 100000 * batched_forward_ms / 1000 / 3600 * overhead, overhead measured), resolve the card's decision rule to if_not: GPU wall-clock for 671 catchments is at least 1 hour, or the GPU beats the CPU by less than 20x
models: GR4J (Perrin, Michel, Andreassian 2003) as implemented by airGR 1.7.9 (committed tarball data/airGR_1.7.9.tar.gz, sha256 7af0d185...b082), re-implemented in JAX with lax.scan over days and chains batched on the leading axis
data: data/L0123001.rda (sha256 e82399bb...afaa): one basin, daily P, E, Qmm, 1984-01-01 to 2012-12-31, from the committed airGR tarball. Timing forcing by committed rule: L0123001 P and E tiled to 2,684 chains x 7,300 days, no noise. No CAMELS data.
arms: anchor_airgr: airGR installed on the box from the committed tarball; RunModel_GR4J with X=(165.05, 6.46, 422.50, 2.45), IndPeriod_Run 1990-01-01..1990-02-28, default warm-up and initial states from CreateRunOptions, ErrorCrit_NSE on Qmm; expected 0.495
anchor_jax: the JAX GR4J on the same inputs and period; NSE and daily flows compared with anchor_airgr
gpu_timing: JAX GPU backend, forward pass over 7,300 days for 268, 1,340 and 2,684 chains; 1 compile warm-up then 10 timed repeats x 3 seeds (seed = tiling offset); median and spread of ms per pass
cpu_timing: JAX CPU backend on the instance's vCPUs, same sizes, same repeats

overhead_probe: 1,000 iterations of batched random-walk Metropolis (Gaussian likelihood on NSE, fixed proposal scale) over 2,684 chains on GPU and on CPU; wall-clock per iteration divided by the forward-pass time is the measured overhead (the card's DESIGN value 4)

endpoints.metric: E1 anchor_airgr NSE on the 59-day run period
endpoints.refuting_outcome: outside the band: the page or period is misread; run stops before timing counts

endpoints.metric: E2 anchor_jax: NSE on the same period, and mean absolute relative error of daily flow versus anchor_airgr over the period
endpoints.refuting_outcome: either fails: the timed model is not GR4J; timing numbers void

endpoints.metric: E3 batched_forward_ms at 2,684 chains on the GPU (median of 30 timed passes)
endpoints.threshold: card guess holds if within [0.67, 6] ms
endpoints.refuting_outcome: median outside [0.67, 6] ms: the card's GUESS is off by more than 3x

endpoints.threshold: card guess holds if within [1, 9] h
endpoints.refuting_outcome: outside [1, 9] h: the card's GUESS is off by more than 3x

endpoints.metric: E5 card decision: main_run_hours = 100000 * batched_forward_ms / 1000 / 3600 * overhead_gpu; speedup = cpu_671_hours / main_run_hours
endpoints.refuting_outcome: main_run_hours < 1 AND speedup >= 20: if_lever; the card's expected outcome is refuted
> 6 h: the card's own text applies, 'Stop and replan: full Bayesian 671 is not affordable on one GPU'

endpoints.metric: E7 scaling: GPU chain-steps per second at 268, 1,340, 2,684 chains
endpoints.threshold: report only; linear if the 2,684/268 throughput ratio is within 20% of 10
endpoints.refuting_outcome: none (descriptive): a ratio well below 10 is reported as 'GPU saturates below 2,684 chains'

sampling: Deterministic model, no decoding. Seeds 1, 2, 3 set the tiling offset of the forcing. 1 compile warm-up pass excluded, then 10 timed passes per seed per size per backend (90 passes per backend). Overhead probe: 1,000 iterations, 2,684 chains, proposal scale 0.05 of each parameter's airGR range, seeds 1-3, GPU and CPU. Every timed pass is written as a raw row; medians are computed from the rows.
does_not_test: Fidelity on real catchments: no CAMELS data (card check 2, 20 catchments within 1%, out of scope). Could be wrong by: the model may be right on L0123001 and still mishandle CAMELS forcing edge cases (missing days, units).
Any posterior quality: no R-hat, no 100,000-iteration run, no point-optimization baseline.
The A6000 the card priced ($1.09/h): the cheapest instance with capacity is used (GUESS at write time: gpu_1x_a10 at $1.29/h, 24 GB); rates and vCPU count recorded from the box.
Implementation alternatives: only lax.scan is timed. A kernel-fused or CUDA-graph implementation could be faster; a Python loop slower. Stated as 'GR4J as a scan on this GPU'.
Memory traffic from real forcing: tiled forcing fits in cache patterns that real data may not.
